episodes.161323: During the afternoon of Thursday, September 16th, a cold front laid across west-central, and central Minnesota. Ahead of this cold front, temperatures soared into the upper 80s to lower 90s. A strong mid-level CAP held through most of the afternoon before a line of clouds started to develop along this front. Storms quickly develop once the CAP broke and with ample wind shear and instability, several of the storms produced large hail, with the largest size measured at 2.5 in diameter. These storms weakened by sunset as they moved slowly eastward toward east central Minnesota.
episodes.161324: A line of thunderstorms that originally developed across South Dakota Thursday evening, September 16th, quickly moved eastward over southern Minnesota after midnight. A series of surges along this line caused localized severe wind gusts that produced numerous downed trees and power lines across southern Minnesota. One of the storms produced an EF0 tornado south of Henderson in far southeast Sibley County. ||As this line moved across the southern Metro of the Twin Cities, three tornadoes briefly spun-up leading to multiple power outages, plus major damage to Savage public works building and a large transformer for the city of Savage. In addition, the power outages caused local schools to close temporarily Friday morning. Another area of tornado damage occurred in Apple Valley and Burnsville. Most of this damage was due to trees falling on houses and vehicles.||A 64 mph wind gust was measured by the ASOS at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. At MSP Airport, with the strong winds and possibly brakes not being applied and/or improper chocking, two Sun Country aircraft slid into each other and into jetways H3 and H4, causing fairly significant damage.||Outside the tornadic activity, several sources of private and public weather sensors measured wind speeds of 40 to 55 mph across a wide swath of southern Minnesota. These winds coupled with heavy rainfall, caused numerous downed small trees and large branches across a 25 to 50 mile wide area from Redwood Falls, to St James, then northeast to New Ulm, Shakopee, St. Paul, and into parts of west central Wisconsin.||In addition, near Mankato, MN around 0730 UTC, a 4-year old girl was killed when a tree branch fell on the tent where she and her family were camping. There were  approximately 80,000 people without power during the peak of the severity that moved through the metro area.
episodes.161328: A line of severe thunderstorms that produced four brief tornadoes, numerous downed trees and power lines across the southern part of the Twin Cities in Minnesota, moved eastward into west-central Wisconsin and produced additional damage near Hudson and west of Roberts. ||One building that sustained significant damage was the Hudson Public Library, where the windows were blown out by debris from the roof a nearby building.
episodes.161402: Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moved across western portions of Lauderdale and Colbert Counties on the 17th, producing widespread rainfall amounts of 3-6 over a few hours. Heavy rainfall also affected Limestone County, both downtown in Decatur, and north, along the AL/TN border again on the 18th. This led to numerous reports of flooding and flash flooding in and around Cherokee, AL, Ardmore, AL, and in Decatur, AL.
episodes.162828: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado during the early evening hours of September 16th. Storms became severe as they crossed the border into Deuel county. Hail up to half dollar size and wind gusts up to 67 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.163010: High pressure across the region promoted light S to SW flow. With ample moisture in place, scattered to numerous showers and storms were able to develop along both the Gulf and Atlantic sea breezes and push towards the east coast metro areas. Heavy rain and flooding were the main hazards.
episodes.163059: A cold front marching across the Northland acted as the catalyst for the development of severe thunderstorms. Storms were initially delayed due to a lingering stratus deck but once convective initiation took hold of the region, the strong ingredients in place lead to numerous severe storms across northeastern Minnesota that produced damaging winds and hail as large as 3 inches in diameter.
episodes.163090: Throughout the day, a cold front moved south across Northwest Kansas. During the morning hours, a line of showers and thunderstorms developed along the front. As the storms moved southeast, a few storms became isolated towards the tail end of the front. One of the isolated storms strengthened over Graham County, producing pea to nickel sized hail south of Hill City.
episodes.163182: A cold front initiated thunderstorms across portions of east central and northeastern South Dakota during the evening of Thursday, September 16th. A couple of these thunderstorms were robust enough to produce large to severe hail.
episodes.163246: An isolated supercell developed across south central South Dakota late evening along an advancing cold frontal boundary.  With appreciable DCAPE and deep-layer effective shear, upscale growth occurred rapidly with the development of widespread damaging winds.
episodes.163247: An isolated supercell developed across south central South Dakota late evening along an advancing cold frontal boundary. With appreciable DCAPE and deep-layer effective shear, upscale growth occurred rapidly with the development of widespread damaging winds, which spread out of eastern South Dakota into Southwest Minnesota.
episodes.163248: An isolated supercell developed across south central South Dakota late evening along an advancing cold frontal boundary. With appreciable DCAPE and deep-layer effective shear, upscale growth occurred rapidly with the development of widespread damaging winds, which spread out of eastern South Dakota into northwest Iowa.
episodes.163251: A line of thunderstorms produced some heavy rain and small hail. One hailstone reached 1 inch in diameter.
episodes.163278: A light flow aloft along with an unstable atmosphere led to slow moving showers and thunderstorms. Heavy amounts of rain led to instances of flooding.
episodes.163384: Heavy rains caused nuisance flooding on the 17th in Barton county.
episodes.163441: Tropical Storm Nicholas made landfall on the Texas coast south of Houston early Tuesday morning on September 14th. As the storm weakened into a remnant low, it slowly meandered across Texas, reaching central Louisiana on the 17th. Outer bands of the remnant low of Nicholas expanded east across coastal Mississippi. The persistent rain from those banding features produced areas of flash flooding.
episodes.163528: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central Virginia.

An EFO tornado touched down near Highway 13 and Connelly Parkway and moved east for 2.1 miles. There was sporadic damage along this path with maximum winds of 85 mph. Most of the damage was due to trees falling on houses and vehicles. The worst damage occurred near the intersection of Connelly Parkway and Dakota Avenue South where roof damage occurred at the Savage Public Works and Light. The city of Savage transformer station also had damage near this intersection, and most of the street lights and signs were damage.

An EF0 tornado touched down near the intersection of Highway 13, and Cliff Road in Burnsville. The path length was approximately 1 mile and most of the damage was due to trees falling on houses and vehicles.

An EF0 tornado touched down near Cedar Avenue and 145th Street West in Apple Valley. The path length was approximately 0.8 miles with a maximum wind speed of 80 mph. Most of the damage was due to trees falling on houses and vehicles.
A semi-trailer flipped over on I-35 north of Highway 19. There was a wind gust of 58 mph near Elko New Market near the time of the incident.

A 64 mph wind gust was measured by the ASOS at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. At MSP Airport, the force of the winds was so strong that two Boeing 737 airplanes belonging to Sun Country Airlines slid into each other and slammed into jet bridges, despite being secured with wheel chocks. There were reports of storm-related damage to other structures, vehicles, and equipment at the airport.
